notes.title: Infinite Voyager's 0.0.4.1 Update is Live!
notes.content: [p]So this one's going to be a little bit shorter, but I have two major updates for this one:[/p][p][/p][h1]Camera Rework[/h1][p][/p][p]The big one is that the camera in starship combat has had a full rework.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/a46ce464590c5196c71d8e6cfc279f347b1d533f.png"][/img][/p][p]Instead of centering around the player's starship, the camera will now zoom in and out to show both starships, allowing you to see your enemy at all times.[/p][p][/p][p]As you move further away from the enemy starship (or vice-versa), the camera will zoom out. Move in closer, and it'll zoom in.[/p][p][/p][p]Keep in mind that this only applies to starships. While I'm open to having it happen for drone combat, I'm partial to having it be more "up-close and personal" to add some variety to the game.[/p][p][/p][h1]Missile Rework[/h1][p][/p][p]The other major update is that the missiles for starships now have a lock-on mechanic, instead of auto-locking immediately.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/c7f3edc91b7f92bc16694fd46b66357075b7243d.png"][/img][/p][p]To lock on to a starship, hover your cursor over the starship until it reaches 100% and turns red. Once this happens, any missiles fired while you're locked on will track towards the enemy starship. Just keep in mind that [i]not[/i] locking on means any fired missiles will shoot in a straight line.[/p][p][/p][h2]AI Missile Rebalancing[/h2][p][/p][p]This one's more of a minor adjustment, but the gist of it is that AI starships will fire missiles less-frequently than before. The time between missile salvos should be doubled to tripled in time to give players more of a break with the larger starships.[/p][p][/p][h2]Frigate rework[/h2][p][/p][p]Long story short, I replaced the Frigate's missiles with a directional autocannon that will fire at the cursor. I'm not opposed to re-adding the missiles, but for now, it'll be a solely-autocannon starship.[/p][p][/p][h1]Conclusion[/h1][p]Anyways, that should do it for this update. Like I said, I'll be devoting more time to developing this game, and I'm really happy with how the camera rework turned out. Be sure to join the Discord to share feedback.[/p][p][/p][p]Have fun![/p][p][/p][p]Chris Providence[/p][p]cGh ONE’s official camara-adjuster[/p][p][/p][h2]Social Media[/h2][p]Web: [url="https://cghone.com/"]https://cghone.com/[/url][/p][p]Bluesky:[url="https://bsky.app/profile/cghone.bsky.social"] [/url][u][url="https://bsky.app/profile/cghone.bsky.social"]@cghone.bsky.social‬[/url][/u][/p][p]YouTube: [dynamiclink href="https://www.youtube.com/@cGh_ONE"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]Discord: [url="https://discord.gg/B5TEdTkEzk"]https://discord.gg/B5TEdTkEzk[/url][/p][p]Twitter: [b]No.[/b][/p]

notes.title: Infinite Voyager's 0.0.4 Update is Live!
notes.content:
[p]It’s been a while, hasn’t it? Yeah, sorry about that.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/2e06d292827386320d17a9e824ea95305343f1d4.png"][/img][/p][p]Turns out it’s a really bad idea to develop multiple games at once when you’re one guy with a dog. But with Tyrannis and the rest of my projects pretty much finished, I can now focus on Infinite Voyager.[/p][p][/p][p]So, let’s get started with what’s new in this (very late) update.[/p][h1]Bug Fixes[/h1][p]Let’s start with some bug fixes:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/93ba3ee23b81ba82f66857a881b9d7e0509fa0ae.png"][/img][/p][list][*][p]Loaded saves will show the correct systems for previously-visited systems.[/p][/*][*][p]The targeting reticule will no longer rotate for smaller ships with point-defense weapons.[/p][/*][*][p]Cursors will show up when they’re supposed to during pause menus.[/p][/*][*][p]The game will no longer crash when entering planets in previously-entered systems.[/p][/*][*][p]Starship shields will now recharge during combat.[/p][/*][*][p]The clock now functions normally instead of going through minutes every second.[/p][/*][/list][h1]Combat Balancing[/h1][p]The big problem, now that I’ve had a chance to look at it, is that combat was just too hard. Which isn’t necessarily a bad thing, except it was too hard on [i]Easy.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]So, after doing some tweaking and rebalancing shield recharge times and health based on difficulty, the enemies should be a bit easier on Easy and Medium, while Hard is still as difficult as ever. More importantly, you can actually tell the difference now.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/2d5654184bd9aa8ec905116957561117d4239b08.png"][/img][/p][p]Another problem I noticed was that missiles during starship combat were pretty much unavoidable if you didn’t have flares. The main strategy of “Wait for your enemy to run out of flares and then hit them with missiles” might be a pragmatic way to win, but it just isn’t fun when you only have ten flares and about twenty missiles gunning for you.[/p][p][/p][p]So starships with flares now have additional flares that won’t run out after a second.[/p][h2]Future Rebalancing[/h2][p]Honestly, I’m looking into removing missiles outright for the starships. They’re pretty much an instant-damage weapon, and outrunning them isn’t too fun. Nothing finalized, but I’m thinking about switching to switching ships out with point defense guns to try and create a more bullet-hell style game that could be more fun.[/p][p][/p][p]Plus, it’d probably be the closest I could get to starships realistically broadsiding each other in space, and that sounds cool as hell.[/p][h1]Drones[/h1][p]But enough about balancing. Let’s talk about Drones.
[/p][p]Drones are basically the new way to handle planetary exploration and battles in [i]Infinite Voyager. [/i]Instead of having a gauntlet of ship battles, you’ll now pilot your drones against squadrons of defense fighters in dogfights around planetary atmospheres.[/p][p][/p][p]Drones can be purchased at any planet’s Drone Depot, and you are only limited by the number of hangars in your starship. If you want to add more hangars, you can now upgrade your starship.[/p][p][/p][p]Now, there are two different types of drones: Recon Drones and Combat Drones.[/p][p][/p][h3]Recon Drones[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/3e214d6b6f85ff4b2b0f8df1778cee302c129c3b.png"][/img][/p][p]Recon Drones are used for planetary exploration. Instead of using your starships, you’ll now use your Drones to explore a planet’s surface. While you will always have a single Recon Drone on you no matter what, it goes without saying that counting planets is a lot faster when you bring more.[/p][h2]Combat Drones[/h2][p]Combat Drones are going to be your new way of fighting in-atmosphere. Not just because I honestly have no idea if these ships would even be rated for atmosphere (as in they won’t explode), but because Combat Drones fight differently than starships.[/p][p][/p][p]Think of it less like a naval battle and more of a dogfight.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/42c46887535b88d73406f3191f055b1513d1cd28.png"][/img][/p][p]There are two different times you’ll be flying a Combat Drone: Trying to access a hostile planet, or trying to take one over.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/2217200c156a08b4c2003c04fdeabe13dd862eaa.png"][/img][/p][p]Combat Drones have similar controls compared to starships. Press Left Shift for boost, the Left Mouse Button for the autocannon, the Middle Mouse Button for flares, and the Right Mouse Button for missiles.[/p][p][/p][p]Assuming you’re locked on, anyways. Otherwise, the missiles will head off to God knows where and keep going.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/0f0ef1bd749faa88ddaeb9c59b831dc7758e6f59.png"][/img][/p][p]Drone Combat works in a series of waves, where your Combat Drone fights increasingly-difficult waves of the planet’s Combat Drones. Destroy one wave, and you’ll have a quick break before you fight the next. Get blown up, and you’ll fly back in with another Combat Drone (assuming you have one).[/p][p][/p][p]Defeat every wave, and you’ll have your victory in the form of access or an entire planet’s worth of loot.[/p][p][/p][p]But if you run out of ships, then you’re back to where you started. Just with fewer Combat Drones.[/p][h1]Conclusion[/h1][p]Anyways, that should conclude this update. Again, sorry for the long delay, but I’ve got a lot more time on my hands right now.[/p][p][/p][p]What’s next? Dunno. Probably the starship weapons rework. Because broadsiding a spaceship with an autocannon sounds cool as hell.[/p][p][/p][p]Until then, take care.
[/p][p]Chris Providence[/p][p]cGh ONE’s one employee[/p][h2]Social Media[/h2][p]Web: [url="https://cghone.com/"]https://cghone.com/[/url][/p][p]Bluesky:[url="https://bsky.app/profile/cghone.bsky.social"] [u]@cghone.bsky.social‬[/u][/url][/p][p]YouTube: [url="https://www.youtube.com/@cGh_ONE"]https://www.youtube.com/@cGh_ONE[/url][/p][p]Discord: [url="https://discord.gg/B5TEdTkEzk"]https://discord.gg/B5TEdTkEzk[/url][/p][p]Twitter: [b]No.[/b][/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Infinite Voyager 0.0.3 Update
notes.content:
So, um... Long time no see, huh?

Okay, if I'm being honest, a big reason why this wasn't going to be updated was [i]Starfield[/i] coming out in 2023. I was honestly scared that nobody would want to play this, since I would be competing against Bethesda (and promptly get my butt kicked because I can't beat them at their own game).

Of course, there's some similarities: "Open-World Space Exploration Game," and all that, but I realized something.

That's about where the similarities end. [i]Infinite Voyager[/i] is its own game that is a love-letter to Sid Meier's Pirates! (except for that freaking dancing mechanic I don't like because I can't see the prompts).

That, and my fundamental game design philosophy is to not compete with other companies by making something truly unique. That way, I don't have to try to beat bigger studios at their own game.

It's that philosophy that helped me design [i]Tyrannis[/i] and [i]Tyrannis: Co-Prosperity[/i], and it's the same philosophy that I'm bringing to Infinite Voyager.

So, with that out of the way, let's take a look at the new updates in 0.0.3:

[list]
[*]Ships can now be upgraded to have drone hangars to carry scouting and combat drones.
[*]Planetary exploration will now be done with drones, instead of ships.
[*]Drones can be purchased planetside.
[*]File size is reduced by removing unused boarding assets.
[*]Readjusted ship costs.
[*]Finally fixed that one bug that was messing with screen resolution.
[*]Reworked planetary invasion gameplay from a gauntlet of ship battles to engaging in dogfights against enemy interceptors in-atmosphere.
[*]Balanced shield recharge for difficulty.
[/list]

Now, updates will be coming out more-often than once a year, but I do have a job now, and I basically make this game in my free time.

But there's a whole lot more to come. It's all in the design phase, but we're looking at more ship upgrades, colonization, shipbuilding, trading, and privateering.

Until then,
Chris Lawrence
Sole Employee at cGh ONE

notes.title: Infinite Voyager 2023 Overhaul Update
notes.content:
Kept you waiting, huh?

Yeah, sorry about that. Had a very hectic 2022, where I nearly died multiple times.

I'm doing better now, though, which means it's time for an update of Infinite Voyager!

[h1]Everything That's Been Updated[/h1]

[h2]True Open-World Gameplay.[/h2]
This time, you aren't going from system to system. Do you see that star over there? Go there and explore the planets. If you want, conquer it for the faction of your choice and come back to it later!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/6c3bcd2fb76a41264a80c065a0d100a73263a0a6.png[/img]

[h2]Combat Interface Changed.[/h2]
One of the problems with combat is that players would have to keep looking away from their ship while they were fighting if they wanted to see if they ran out of ammo. Sure, that works in FPS games, but this is a roguelike space exploration game, not an FPS. Better to have all the info you need right next to your ship.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/3c8a2e53a5eaab84668d983c5872bedd68beba91.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/505ab631bc23c106712947549d9fa53dd60afa53.png[/img]

[h2]UI Overhaul[/h2]
I'll be honest, this one is kind of for me. Sure, the old look wasn't bad, but man did it look ugly. A fresh coat of neon-blue paint looks way better.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/0184b6b51d8d8ff4c6a5e84ae3eba45b37d92f30.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/07e93eb9c6b4f54d9a0986546b841f24ebfa9c16.png[/img]

[h2]Ledger Fix[/h2]
Want to keep track of everything you have in total? Now there's a tab for that.

And they show up!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/5dc99aa5e3805280cb0cd590f51c69173b62d3cf.png[/img]

[h2]Save System Overhaul[/h2]
If you're going to be traveling through an entire galaxy, then you're going to need a new save system to save all that progress. Now you have one!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/3569b37c8cedacf12bfdc85649402b6dba277b25.png[/img]

[h2]Tutorial Overhaul[/h2]
Inspired by Tyrannis' own video tutorials, I've basically gutted the old text-based tutorial system and replaced it with a brand-new video tutorial.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/2d790c33e3a7720fec5183979408ccfab30b1f90.png[/img]

[h2]Planet Defense Fleet Fix[/h2]
Are you tired of attacking a system, only to have to retreat, then return to an entirely new defense fleet? Well, that's all a thing of the past, now. When you attack a ship in the defense fleet, it's going to stay dead or captured.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/b25a72e9a8e2cd90737a3da794a6ef3b411c5465.png[/img]

And we're just getting started, folks.

Anyways, it's good to be back and working on Infinite Voyager again. Updates should be coming more regularly now.

Thanks to everyone who helped bring the game here. Seriously, I couldn't do it without you guys.

It's good to be back.

-Chris

notes.content:
Glad to see so many people interested in Infinite Voyager this week!

notes.title: February 5 Hotfix Notes
notes.content:
24 hours in, and I've gotten some constructive feedback from you all about Infinite Voyager. Keep it coming.

I get it. Scanning planets isn't the most fun thing to do in the galaxy. Not when you can fly around and commit space piracy.

[b]So, I've done a few things to make it worth your while:[/b]
[list]
[*]Increased scanning speed and flight speed when exploring.
[*]Ships will now remain in-orbit and deploy their Aeternus Type-381 "Galaxy" drone to scout planets.
[*]The Aeternus Type-381 Galaxy can detect jettisoned cargo, resource deposits, and credit pods.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41820605/0184b6b51d8d8ff4c6a5e84ae3eba45b37d92f30.png[/img]

[b]In addition, there are a few fixes for glitches that've been reported:[/b]
[list]
[*]When saving, ghost ships will no longer appear to crash your game.
[*]The AI controlling combat ships will no longer pursue you unless you've done something to anger them enough to attack you.
[*]In the unexplored systems, that includes existing.
[/list]
Anyways, I hope you all are having fun with Infinite Voyager.

And remember: [b]It will always be ethical to steal from the Aeternus Corporation.[/b]

-Chris
